ai.description: This small skink reaches 5 cm snout-vent length. It features a dark brown body with a distinct pale dorsolateral stripe and a reddish-brown tail. Key traits include a translucent lower eyelid window.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kaestlea beddomii* is best distinguished from similar skinks by the presence of a distinct, continuous pale dorsolateral stripe that extends from the snout to the tail.
ai.habitat: *Kaestlea beddomii* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome's Ground Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kaestlea beddomii* is oviparous, laying a small clutch of 2–3 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Kaestlea beddomii* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in high-elevation montane forests and grasslands across Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
